findings.summary: Encryption /P is -4 instead of -1796, so requested permission restrictions are not applied
findings.description:
## Affected

`github.com/malcolmston/pdfkit` `<= v0.0.0-20260810111600-857c462c84f5`, `Doc.Encrypt` / `EncryptOptions`. Parity cases **`enc-all-permissions`** and **`enc-aes-128`** (`parity/pdfkit/cases/encryption.json`), recorded as divergence **3** in `parity/pdfkit/COVERAGE.md`. Upstream oracle: `pdfkit@0.15.1`.

## Upstream vs port behaviour

For the same requested permissions, the two implementations write different `/P` values into the encryption dictionary:

| | `/P` |
| --- | --- |
| upstream `pdfkit@0.15.1` | **-1796** |
| this port | **-4** |

Two independent mistakes produce that:

1. **Unrequestable bits are left set.** The port never clears the form-filling (bit 9), content-accessibility (bit 10) and document-assembly (bit 11) bits. `EncryptOptions` has no flag for any of them — `COVERAGE.md` rows `options.permissions.fillingForms`, `.contentAccessibility`, `.documentAssembly` are all `missing` — and the implementation sets them unconditionally.
2. **The reserved-bit base mask is not applied.** Upstream's `getPermissionsR3` starts from `0xfffff0c0` (the PDF spec's "reserved bits must be 1, bits 1-2 must be 0" base) and clears the bits the caller denied. The port does not, so the reserved-bit pattern is wrong in addition to the permission bits.

## Impact

`/P` is the document permission policy. A caller who writes

```go
doc.Encrypt(pdfkit.EncryptOptions{
    OwnerPassword:    "owner",
    AllowPrinting:    false,
    AllowModify:      false,
    AllowCopying:     false,
    AllowAnnotations: false,
})
```

reasonably believes the document is locked down. What is actually written grants form filling, text extraction for accessibility, and document assembly (page insert / delete / rotate / reorder) to every reader, regardless of what was requested. In particular the content-accessibility bit is the text-extraction-for-screen-readers bit, so text can be extracted from a document whose author explicitly denied copying; and document assembly permits reordering or deleting pages of a document whose author denied modification. Nothing warns: the file encrypts, opens, and reports itself protected — only the policy is wrong. Because the bits are not expressible in `EncryptOptions` at all, there is no workaround available to the caller.

**Severity: low, deliberately.** PDF permission flags have never been a real security boundary. They are advisory: enforcement lives entirely in the viewer, every conforming reader can ignore them, the user already holds the decryption key for a document opened without a user password, and freely available tooling strips them. This is a correctness failure to apply a restriction the author asked for, and a violation of the caller's stated intent, not a break of a control that could otherwise have been relied on. It is being tracked as a security advisory because the affected API is one callers reach for specifically to restrict sensitive documents, and because it fails silently — not because the resulting exposure is strong. It should not be presented as stronger than it is.

## Repro

```go
doc := pdfkit.New()
doc.AddPage(pdfkit.A4)
doc.Encrypt(pdfkit.EncryptOptions{OwnerPassword: "o"}) // deny everything
b, _ := doc.Bytes()
// inspect the /Encrypt dictionary: /P -4   (upstream for the same input: /P -1796)
```

Harness: `GOWORK=off go test ./parity/pdfkit/`

## Fix

Port upstream's computation directly: start from the base mask `0xfffff0c0`, clear one bit per denied permission, and serialise the result interpreted as a signed 32-bit integer. Add the three missing permission flags (`AllowFillingForms`, `AllowContentAccessibility`, `AllowDocumentAssembly`) so the policy is expressible at all, and consider defaulting them to denied when the caller supplies an explicit permission set. Note that upstream's `printing` is tri-state (`false` / `"lowResolution"` / `"highResolution"`) rather than boolean, which also affects `/P`; that gap is tracked separately as a missing-API issue.
